lessons.title: Reading · Grandma's paper-cutting
lessons.en:
My grandma is 78. Her hands are thin and wrinkled, but they can do magic. She is a master of paper-cutting.

She learned the skill at eight from her mother. At first she only cut simple shapes — a flower, a star, a fish. By fifteen, she could cut a dragon with every scale clear. Every Spring Festival, our neighbours come to ask her for window flowers.

Last winter, Grandma taught me. She gave me a soft red paper and small scissors. “Hold the paper loosely and move the scissors slowly. Feel the paper like a friend,” she said.

My first rabbit had a broken ear; my second rabbit had three legs. Grandma laughed, but she was patient. By my tenth try, my rabbit looked like a rabbit at last!

Grandma says, “A skill is like a seed. If nobody plants it, it dies.” I am glad I am a small planter now.
lessons.cn:
奶奶 78 岁了，手瘦又布满皱纹，却能变魔术——她是剪纸大师。

她 8 岁跟母亲学艺，起初只会剪花、星、鱼；15 岁能剪出鳞片分明的龙。每逢春节，邻居都来求她剪窗花。

去年冬天奶奶教我。她递给我柔软红纸和小剪刀，说：“纸要捏松、剪要慢，把纸当朋友。”

我剪的第一只兔子耳朵断了，第二只三条腿，奶奶笑着仍耐心指导。第十次时，我的兔子终于像兔子了！

奶奶说：“技艺像种子，没人种下就会死。”我很高兴自己成了一个小小的播种人。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Used to / be used to
lessons.en:
1) used to + verb — a past habit that is NOT true now.
Grandma used to cut paper every morning.
I used to be afraid of the dark.
Did you use to play with paper? — Yes, I did.

2) be used to + verb-ing (or noun) — be familiar with.
She is used to getting up early.
I am used to the cold weather now.

3) be used to + verb — be USED FOR a purpose (passive).
Scissors are used to cut paper.
Knives are used to cut fruits.

Compare:
used to cut paper = past habit
is used to cutting paper = is familiar with cutting
is used to cut paper = is used for cutting
lessons.cn:
1) used to + 动词原形——过去习惯（现在不再如此）：
奶奶过去每天早上剪纸。
我过去怕黑。
你过去常玩纸吗？——是的。

2) be used to + v-ing（或名词）——习惯于：
她习惯早起。
我现在习惯冷天了。

3) be used to + 动词原形——被用来做某事（被动）：
剪刀被用来剪纸。
刀被用来切水果。

对比：
used to cut paper = 过去常剪
is used to cutting paper = 习惯剪
is used to cut paper = 被用来剪

lessons.title: More reading · Why save old skills?
lessons.en:
Our country has thousands of traditional skills — embroidery from Suzhou, porcelain from Jingdezhen, kites from Weifang, tea from Hangzhou. Each skill tells a story of the land and its people.

But today, many are in danger. Young people move to cities to find office jobs. Old masters grow old with no students. When the last master passes away, the skill may disappear forever.

Why should we save them? First, they are our heritage — our grandparents' wisdom is in every stitch and knot. Second, they bring beauty into daily life; a handmade tea cup feels warm in a way a factory cup never does. Third, they help poor villages — tourists love handmade souvenirs.

Today many schools open “culture clubs” for children to learn old crafts. Young people share short videos of paper-cutting and calligraphy online, with millions of fans. The river of tradition keeps flowing as long as someone, somewhere, keeps it alive.
lessons.cn:
我国有成千上万项传统技艺：苏州刺绣、景德镇瓷器、潍坊风筝、杭州茶艺——每一项都讲述土地与人的故事。

但如今许多技艺濒危：年轻人进城找办公室工作，老师傅无人传承。最后一位大师一旦去世，技艺可能永远失传。

为什么要保护？一、它们是遗产——爷爷奶奶的智慧藏在每一针、每一结里。二、它们让日常生活充满美——手工茶杯的温度，机器杯永远没有。三、它们能帮贫困乡村——游客热衷手工纪念品。

如今许多学校开设“文化社团”让孩子学老手艺；年轻人在网络上分享剪纸、书法短视频，粉丝百万。只要有人在某处让它继续跳动，传统之河就会奔流不息。

lessons.title: Reading · My robot friend
lessons.en:
Last Christmas, my uncle gave me an unusual present — a small white robot called Buddy. Buddy is only 30 centimetres tall but he can do many things.

In the morning, Buddy wakes me up with a soft song, tells me the weather and reads the news in English. While I brush my teeth, he moves around my bed and picks up dirty socks.

When I do homework, Buddy sits quietly on my desk. If I ask a hard math question, his eyes turn blue and he gives a clear answer. Sometimes he even makes a small joke.

But Buddy is not perfect. He does not like water — one rainy day he ran outside by mistake, and I had to dry him for an hour. He also has a weak battery, so he must rest for two hours every afternoon.

I know Buddy is just a machine, but I enjoy his company. He reminds me that science can be both useful and fun.
lessons.cn:
去年圣诞叔叔送我一个特别礼物——30 厘米高的白色小机器人 Buddy，本领可不小。

早晨 Buddy 用柔和歌曲叫我起床、告诉我天气、用英语读新闻。我刷牙时他绕床把脏袜子拾起。

我写作业时他静静坐在桌上。如果我问难题，他双眼会变蓝给出清晰答案，有时还讲个小笑话。

但 Buddy 并不完美：他怕水——一个雨天跑出去，我给他擦了一小时；电池弱，每天下午得“午睡”两小时。

我知道他只是机器，但我喜欢他的陪伴。他让我明白：科技既有用又好玩。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · First conditional (future if)
lessons.en:
First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb.
Use it for a real, possible future.

If I press this button, the robot will sing.
If you take care of Buddy, he will stay with you for years.
If the battery runs out, the robot won't move.

Order can be reversed (no comma then):
The robot will sing if I press this button.
Buddy won't move if the battery runs out.

Unless = if ... not:
Unless you charge it, the robot won't start.
= If you don't charge it, the robot won't start.

Tip: DON'T use will in the if clause.
✗ If I will press this button...
✓ If I press this button...
lessons.cn:
第一条件句：if + 一般现在时，主句 will + 动词。
用于真实可能发生的未来。

我按这个键，机器人就唱歌。
你好好照顾 Buddy，他会陪你很多年。
电用完机器人就不动了。

前后可以调换（无逗号）：
The robot will sing if I press this button.
Buddy won't move if the battery runs out.

unless = if ... not：
除非你充电，机器人不会启动。
= 如果你不充电，机器人不会启动。

提示：if 从句里绝不用 will。
✗ If I will press this button...
✓ If I press this button...

lessons.title: More reading · Robots at work
lessons.en:
Robots are no longer in science-fiction films. They are already working all around us.

In factories, robot arms build cars, pack milk and sort packages day and night. One car factory in Guangzhou has 900 robot arms working with 200 human workers. In hospitals, small robots help doctors do careful operations, and some deliver medicine from room to room. In restaurants, a robot waiter carries soup from the kitchen to your table. At home, a robot vacuum cleaner sweeps the floor while you watch TV.

But robots cannot do everything. They cannot comfort a sad friend. They cannot write a poem from the heart. They cannot decide what is right or wrong in hard situations.

The future is not humans OR robots. It is humans AND robots — each doing what they do best.
lessons.cn:
机器人不再只在科幻片里，它们早已走进我们身边。

工厂里：机械臂昼夜组装汽车、包装牛奶、分拣快件。广州一家汽车厂有 900 台机械臂与 200 名工人协作。医院里：小机器人协助医生做精细手术，一些机器人在病房间送药。餐馆里机器人从厨房端汤到餐桌；家里扫地机器人在你看电视时清洁地板。

但机器人不是万能——安慰伤心朋友、写发自内心的诗、在困境中判断是非，这些仍需要人。

未来不是人 VS 机器人，而是人 + 机器人——各展所长，共创未来。

lessons.title: Reading · A visit to Sanjiangyuan
lessons.en:
Last summer my family joined a five-day nature trip to Sanjiangyuan in Qinghai — the source of the Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang rivers.

Sanjiangyuan is home to many rare animals — snow leopards, Tibetan antelopes, black-necked cranes and brown bears. Because of hunting and climate change, their numbers dropped sharply in the last century.

Today, things are changing. Since 2000, the Chinese government has set up large reserves. Over 3,000 rangers ride horses day and night to protect the animals. The Tibetan antelope population went from 20,000 in the 1990s to over 70,000 today.

On the third morning, our guide pointed to a hill. Far away, a group of Tibetan antelopes were running in the sunshine. Nobody spoke. We just watched quietly.

At that moment, I understood: protecting animals is protecting a story that has been going on for millions of years, and must not end on our watch.
lessons.cn:
去年夏天我家参加了青海三江源五日自然之旅——这里是长江、黄河、澜沧江的源头。

三江源是许多珍稀动物的家园：雪豹、藏羚羊、黑颈鹤、棕熊。因过度狩猎和气候变化，上世纪它们数量骤减。

如今情况在好转。自 2000 年起中国政府建立大型保护区，3000 多名巡护员昼夜骑马守护动物。藏羚羊从上世纪 90 年代的 2 万只回升到今天的 7 万多只。

第三天清晨向导指向远处山坡——一群藏羚羊在阳光下奔跑。没人说话，我们静静注视。

那一刻我明白：保护动物就是保护一个已存续了数百万年的故事，这故事不能终结于我们这代人。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Present perfect with since / for
lessons.en:
Present perfect: have/has + past participle. Use it for actions that started in the past and continue to now.

for + period: for ten years, for a long time.
I have studied English for six years.
The government has protected pandas for many decades.

since + point in time: since 2000, since Monday, since I was a child.
She has lived here since 2010.
I have loved animals since I was three.

Questions:
How long have you studied English?
— I have studied it for six years.
— I have studied it since Grade 3.

Note: use present perfect (not simple past) with for/since in this meaning.
✗ I studied English for six years. (you stopped)
✓ I have studied English for six years. (still learning)
lessons.cn:
现在完成时：have/has + 过去分词，表过去开始、延续至今的动作。

for + 一段时间：for ten years, for a long time。
我学英语六年了。
政府保护熊猫数十年了。

since + 时间点：since 2000, since Monday, since I was a child。
她自 2010 年住在这里。
我从三岁起就爱动物。

问句：
你学英语多久了？
——六年。
——从三年级起。

注意：表延续性意义必须用现在完成时，不能用一般过去时。
✗ I studied English for six years.（停了）
✓ I have studied English for six years.（仍在学）

lessons.title: More reading · What kids can do
lessons.en:
You might think saving wildlife is a job for scientists and governments. But children can help too.

1) Learn and share. Read about endangered animals. Tell your family the interesting facts. Knowledge is the first step to action.

2) Never buy products from wild animals. Ivory, tiger bones, rare fur and shark fins — say no to them all. If people stop buying, poachers stop hunting.

3) Support a reserve. Many panda or sea-turtle reserves let children adopt an animal with a small donation. In return, you get photos and stories.

4) Be a green tourist. At a zoo or park, don't feed the animals without permission. Don't shout or throw rubbish. Walk softly, watch quietly.

Your hands are small, but thousands of small hands together can protect a forest. Every kind thought counts.
lessons.cn:
你可能以为保护野生动物是科学家和政府的事，孩子其实也能出力。

1) 学习并分享。多读濒危动物资料，把有趣知识讲给家人。知识是行动的第一步。

2) 绝不购买野生动物制品——象牙、虎骨、稀有皮毛、鱼翅通通说不。买家消失，偷猎者也就消失。

3) 支持保护区。许多熊猫、海龟保护区可用小额捐款“领养”动物，回赠照片和故事。

4) 做绿色游客。在动物园或公园未经许可不喂食；不喧哗、不乱扔垃圾；轻步安静观察。

你的手很小，千双小手合力就能守护一片森林。每一份善念都很重要。

Plant the seed in good soil.

lessons.title: Reading · A little gardener
lessons.en:
When I was six, my grandfather gave me a small flower pot and a few tomato seeds. That was my first garden.

He told me three secrets. First, plants need good soil — not too dry and not too wet. Second, plants love sunlight, so put the pot where the morning sun can reach. Third, plants are like children — they need love and patience.

I watered the seeds every day and checked them every hour. On the seventh morning, I saw two tiny green leaves! I shouted so loud that the whole family came running.

Three months later, I had ten shining red tomatoes. Mum made a salad, and we all ate the tomatoes I had grown. It tasted like sunshine.

I am fourteen now. I have a larger garden on our balcony — lettuce, chilli peppers, mint and even a small lemon tree. Plants have taught me that slow is beautiful, kindness grows life, and every seed carries a whole story inside.
lessons.cn:
六岁时爷爷给我一个小花盆和几粒番茄种子——那是我的第一座花园。

他告诉我三个秘诀：一、土要适中——不能太干也不能太湿；二、植物爱阳光，把盆放在能晒到早晨太阳的地方；三、植物像孩子，需要耐心和关爱。

我每天浇水，每小时都去看。第七天早上看到两片嫩绿小叶！我大叫，全家都跑来了。

三个月后，我收获 10 颗红番茄。妈妈做了沙拉，全家一起品尝——尝起来像阳光。

如今我 14 岁，阳台上有更大的花园——生菜、辣椒、薄荷，甚至一棵小柠檬树。植物教了我：慢也是美丽，善意孕育生命，每一粒种子里都藏着一整个故事。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Reflexive pronouns
lessons.en:
Reflexive pronouns end in -self / -selves.

I → myself       We → ourselves
You → yourself   You → yourselves
He → himself     They → themselves
She → herself
It → itself

Use 1 — action returns to the doer:
I watered the plants by myself.
The cat washes itself every day.
We taught ourselves to cook.

Use 2 — emphasis:
Grandpa himself showed me the secret.
The flowers themselves were very small.

Fixed phrases:
by myself = alone.
enjoy yourself = have a good time.
help yourself = take what you want.

Examples:
She grew the tomatoes by herself.
Enjoy yourselves at the garden party!
Please help yourself to some salad.
lessons.cn:
反身代词以 -self/-selves 结尾。

我 → myself        我们 → ourselves
你 → yourself      你们 → yourselves
他 → himself       他们 → themselves
她 → herself
它 → itself

用法 1——动作回到自己：
我独自浇花。
猫每天自己梳洗。
我们自学做饭。

用法 2——强调：
爷爷亲自告诉我秘诀。
花本身很小。

固定短语：
by myself = 独自。
enjoy yourself = 玩得开心。
help yourself = 请自便取用。

例：
她独自种番茄。
在花园派对上玩得开心！
请自便吃点沙拉。

lessons.title: More reading · Green doctors
lessons.en:
Plants are our oldest doctors. For thousands of years, people have used plants to cure illnesses.

In ancient China, Li Shizhen travelled across the country for 27 years and recorded 1,892 kinds of plants, animals and minerals in Bencao Gangmu — a book still studied today.

Modern science has proved many plant medicines. The willow tree gives us aspirin. The Pacific yew helps cancer patients. Chinese scientist Tu Youyou found a medicine from a small plant called qinghao. Her medicine has saved millions of lives from malaria. In 2015, she won the Nobel Prize.

But many plant species are disappearing. A forest may contain a plant that could cure a future illness. If the plant dies before we find it, that hope dies too.

That is why we must protect rainforests, mountains and even city parks. Every plant is a page in the green book of life. Lose the page, and the story is gone forever.
lessons.cn:
植物是我们最古老的医生。几千年来人们一直用植物治病。

古代中国李时珍跋山涉水 27 年，在《本草纲目》中记录 1892 种植物、动物和矿物——至今仍被医生研读。

现代科学证实许多药物来自植物：柳树给了我们阿司匹林，太平洋紫杉帮助癌症患者。中国科学家屠呦呦从青蒿中发现药物，挽救了数百万疟疾患者的生命，2015 年荣获诺贝尔奖。

但许多植物物种正在消失。一片森林里可能藏着某种植物能治未来的疾病；若植物先于发现而消亡，希望也会跟着消失。

这也是为什么要保护雨林、山地，甚至城市公园。每一株植物都是“绿色生命之书”中的一页。失去一页，故事便永久中断。

words.example: The moon shines at night.
The Earth is round.
The moon orbits the Earth.
The moon has weak gravity.
A rocket carries astronauts.
The astronaut walked on the moon.
China's spacecraft landed on Mars.
The moon's surface has craters.
There are huge craters on the moon.
China landed on the dark side of the moon.
The rocket will launch at dawn.
Humans love to explore space.
The Chang'e mission brought moon rocks back.
Chang'e-5 returned to Earth in 2020.
Humans have dreamed of the moon for thousands of years.

lessons.title: Reading · A journey to the moon
lessons.en:
For thousands of years, people have looked up at the moon and dreamed. In ancient China there was a lovely story of Chang'e flying to the moon with a small white rabbit. But it was only a story.

Everything changed in 1969. Two American astronauts became the first humans to walk on the moon. Half a century later, in 2020, China's Chang'e-5 landed on the moon, collected 1.7 kilograms of moon rocks and returned safely. In 2024, Chang'e-6 went to the far (dark) side of the moon — the first mission in history to bring back rocks from that mysterious place.

The moon is 384,000 kilometres from Earth, but the trip takes about four days. There is no air, no rain, no wind and no sound. Daytime surface reaches 127°C; at night it falls to −173°C. An astronaut's suit is like a small spaceship.

From dream to footprint, from footprint to rocks in the lab — humans have come a long way. The next step might be Mars.
lessons.cn:
几千年来人们仰望月亮，怀着梦想。古代中国有嫦娥抱玉兔奔月的传说，但那长时间只是故事。

1969 年一切改变——两位美国宇航员成为踏上月球的第一批人类。半世纪后的 2020 年，中国嫦娥五号登月采回 1.7 公斤月壤并安全返航；2024 年嫦娥六号更进一步，前往月球背面，成为人类史上首次从月背取样返回的任务。

月球距地球 38.4 万公里，依然要飞行约 4 天。那里没有空气、雨水、风和声音；白天地表 127℃，夜晚 −173℃。宇航服就像一艘小型飞船。

从梦想到脚印，从脚印到实验室里的月岩——人类一路走来。下一站或许是火星。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Modal verbs of possibility
lessons.en:
Use modal verbs to show how sure you are:

must + verb → very sure (~95%):
The rocket must be ready. The engines are hot.
He must be an astronaut; he has the suit.

may / might + verb → possible (~50%):
It may rain tomorrow, so the launch may be delayed.
There might be water on the dark side of the moon.

could + verb → possible (a little less sure):
We could reach Mars in twenty years.
There could be life on other planets.

can't + verb → very sure it is NOT:
That can't be the moon; it is too small.
You can't be a real astronaut — you are only thirteen!

Tips:
- No "to" after these modals: must go (✓), must to go (✗).
- "must" for guesses; "have to" for obligations.
lessons.cn:
情态动词表达确信程度：

must——很确定（约 95%）：
火箭肯定已就绪——发动机发烫了。
他一定是宇航员，身上有航天服。

may / might——有可能（约 50%）：
明天可能下雨，发射也许推迟。
月球背面可能有水。

could——可能（比 may 略弱）：
二十年内也许能登陆火星。
其他行星上可能有生命。

can't——很确定“不是”：
那不可能是月亮，太小了。
你不可能是真宇航员——才 13 岁！

注意：
- 情态动词后不加 to：must go（✓），must to go（✗）。
- must 表猜测；have to 表义务。

lessons.title: More reading · Future cities on the moon
lessons.en:
What will life on the moon be like? Scientists are already drawing plans for the first moon bases.

A moon base will probably be built inside a large crater — the crater walls can block dangerous radiation from the Sun. Another good place is a lava tube, a natural tunnel under the surface. Some tubes are so big that a small town could fit inside.

Energy will come from the Sun. Huge solar panels will catch sunlight. Water may come from ice frozen deep in the moon's south pole. Food will grow inside glass greenhouses. Rice, lettuce and tomatoes have already grown in space stations.

Of course, there are still problems. The moon has only one-sixth of Earth's gravity. After six months the human body becomes weaker. We will need special exercise machines every day.

You are fourteen today. By the time you are forty, humans may live on the moon. And who knows — you might be one of them.
lessons.cn:
月球上的生活会是什么样？科学家已在为首个月球基地绘制蓝图。

基地可能建在大型陨石坑里——坑壁可挡住危险的太阳辐射；另一个理想地点是月表之下的天然熔岩管道，有些管道大到可容纳一整个小城。

能源来自太阳——巨型光伏板吸收阳光。水可能来自月球南极深处的冰。食物在玻璃温室里种植——稻米、生菜、番茄已在空间站成功生长。

当然挑战重重：月球引力只有地球的六分之一，半年后人体会变弱，每天都需要特殊锻炼器械。

你今年 14 岁，当你 40 岁时，人类也许已在月球生活。——谁知道呢，你或许就是其中之一。

words.example: We live a green life.
Protect the environment.
Air pollution harms our lungs.
Climate change is a real problem.
Global warming is serious.
Recycle paper, plastic and glass.
Reuse the plastic bags.
Reduce plastic waste.
Plastic takes 400 years to break down.
Don't drop rubbish on the ground.
Sort your rubbish every day.
We must reduce carbon emissions.
Leave a small carbon footprint.
Solar is a renewable energy.
We share the responsibility to protect Earth.

lessons.title: Reading · A green month at our school
lessons.en:
Last month our school held a Green Month. Every class had to find a green idea and put it into action.

Our class chose Zero Plastic Lunch. Instead of disposable boxes, each student brought a glass or metal lunchbox from home, and our own spoons, chopsticks and water bottles. By the end of the first week we had saved over 600 plastic boxes!

Class Three started a paper hospital. They collected old exercise books, pulled out any clean pages, and sewed them into new notebooks. The notebooks were given to a village school in Guangxi.

Class Seven built a green corner on the balcony with mint, basil and small tomato plants. On Wednesday afternoons, everyone could take a leaf home.

Most creative was Class Five — on Saturday they made a second-hand market selling old toys, books and shoes. The money (1,856 yuan) went to an animal reserve in Yunnan.

Green Month taught us that saving the Earth is not one big act. It is many small ones, done by many small hands, every day.
lessons.cn:
上个月我校举办“绿色之月”，每班须想出一个环保点子并付诸行动。

我们班选了“零塑午餐”：不用一次性餐盒，每人从家带玻璃或金属饭盒、勺子、筷子和水杯。第一周就省下 600 多个塑料盒！

三班办起“纸张医院”：收集旧作业本，抽出干净的页，缝成新笔记本送给广西山区小学。

七班在阳台打造绿色小角，种薄荷、罗勒和小番茄苗。每周三下午大家都能摘一片叶子回家。

最富创意的是五班——周六办跳蚤市场，同学卖旧玩具、旧书、旧鞋，筹得 1856 元全数捐给云南一家动物保护区。

“绿色之月”让我们明白：拯救地球不是一件大事，而是许多双小手天天做的许多小事。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Should / ought to / had better
lessons.en:
Three common ways to give suggestions:

1) should + verb (most common, neutral):
We should plant more trees.
You shouldn't waste water.
Should I take a cloth bag? — Yes, you should.

2) ought to + verb (slightly stronger, a moral duty):
We ought to protect the Earth.
People ought to respect wildlife.
Negative: ought not to / oughtn't to.

3) had better + verb (a warning, strong hint):
You had better save water, or the bill will be high.
We had better leave now; it is getting dark.
Negative: had better not + verb.

Compare:
should = my good advice
ought to = society's expectation
had better = a warning, stronger than the other two
lessons.cn:
提建议常用三种结构：

1) should + 动词（最常用，中性）：
我们应该多种树。
你不应该浪费水。
我该带布袋吗？——该。

2) ought to + 动词（稍强，道义上应该）：
我们应当保护地球。
人们应当尊重野生动物。
否定：ought not to / oughtn't to。

3) had better + 动词（警告 / 强烈建议）：
你最好节约水，不然账单会高。
我们最好现在走，天要黑了。
否定：had better not + 动词。

对比：
should = 我的好建议
ought to = 社会普遍期望
had better = 语气更强的警告

lessons.title: More reading · Small steps, big world
lessons.en:
Climate change sounds huge — forests on fire, ice melting, oceans rising. But the biggest journey starts with a single step. Here are five small steps every student can take:

1) Walk or cycle when the trip is short. A 2-kilometre walk saves about half a kilogram of carbon.

2) Turn off lights, computers and chargers when you leave a room. Don't let them sleep — switch them off.

3) Eat local food. Apples from a nearby orchard travel 20 kilometres; oranges from another country travel 20,000.

4) Sort your rubbish. Paper, metal, plastic and kitchen waste all go to different bins. Proper sorting cuts the rubbish that goes to landfill by half.

5) Plant something — even a mint leaf on your windowsill. Green life cleans the air and makes you smile.

A single person can't save the world. But a single person can change one home. A hundred homes can change a street. A million streets can change a planet.
lessons.cn:
气候变化听来巨大——森林大火、冰川融化、海平面上升。但最长的旅程始于一步。学生可走五小步：

1) 短途步行或骑车。2 公里步行约少排 0.5 公斤碳。

2) 离开房间关灯、关电脑、拔充电器——别让它们“睡觉”，直接关机。

3) 吃本地食物。附近果园的苹果跑 20 公里，进口橙子跑 2 万公里。

4) 垃圾分类。纸、金、塑、厨余各自分箱。分好后送去填埋的垃圾能减少一半。

5) 种点东西——哪怕窗台上一株薄荷。绿色生命净化空气，也让你微笑。

一个人救不了世界，却能改变一个家；百家能改变一条街；百万街道能改变一颗星球。

words.example: Confucius was a genius whose ideas still shape China today.
The ancient Greek philosopher Socrates asked more questions than he answered.
Confucius' influence can still be felt in modern classrooms.
Honesty is a virtue that never goes out of fashion.
He showed respect to both his parents and his teachers.
Old sayings often carry the wisdom of many generations.
Confucius had about 3,000 disciples, but only 72 became masters themselves.
She is a scholar of ancient Chinese literature.
Although he won the Nobel Prize, he remained humble.
A famous quote from Confucius is about learning and thinking.
Ancient scrolls were kept carefully in the palace library.
The Tang Dynasty was a golden age for Chinese poetry.
As a thinker, he dared to ask questions that others avoided.
Knowledge without practice is like a tree without fruit.
His greatest legacy is a set of ideas about kindness and learning.

lessons.title: Reading · A talk about Confucius
lessons.en:
Mr Li: Good morning, everyone. Today we are going to talk about one of the wisest men in Chinese history — Confucius.

Anna: Mr Li, when was Confucius born?

Mr Li: He was born in 551 BC, in the State of Lu — today's Shandong Province. That's more than 2,500 years ago!

Tom: What did he do for a living?

Mr Li: He was a teacher, a thinker and a government officer. But most of all, he was a great teacher. He believed that every person, rich or poor, had the right to learn.

Anna: My grandma often says, "Learning without thinking is useless." Did Confucius say that?

Mr Li: Yes! The full quote is, "Learning without thinking is useless; thinking without learning is dangerous." It is still very true today.

Tom: Did he have many students?

Mr Li: About three thousand. Seventy-two of them became famous teachers themselves. Together with his disciples, he wrote a book called The Analects.

Anna: What did he teach about?

Mr Li: Virtue, respect, honesty and kindness. He believed a good person first tries to fix himself, then his family, and only then his country.

Tom: That sounds like something a modern teacher would say!

Mr Li: That is why we call him a wise man. A wise man's words never grow old.
lessons.cn:
李老师：早上好，同学们。今天我们来聊聊中国历史上最有智慧的人之一——孔子。

安娜：李老师，孔子是什么时候出生的？

李老师：他生于公元前 551 年，出生在鲁国，也就是今天的山东省，距今两千五百多年！

汤姆：他做什么工作？

李老师：他是老师、思想家，也当过官。但最重要的身份是伟大的老师。他认为无论贫富，每个人都有受教育的权利。

安娜：我奶奶常说：“学而不思则罔。”这是孔子的话吗？

李老师：是的！完整的句子是：“学而不思则罔，思而不学则殆。”今天依然很有道理。

汤姆：他有很多学生吗？

李老师：约三千弟子，其中七十二人后来成了著名的老师。他和弟子一起编成了《论语》。

安娜：他主要教什么？

李老师：仁、礼、诚、善。他认为做好人先从修身做起，再到齐家，最后才是治国。

汤姆：听起来像现代老师会说的话！

李老师：这就是为什么称他为圣人——智者的话永远不过时。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Defining relative clauses with who / which / that
lessons.en:
A defining relative clause tells us which person or thing we are talking about. It usually follows a noun.

1) who — for people
   The teacher who wrote this book is from Shanghai.
   Confucius is the philosopher who believed in lifelong learning.

2) which — for things and animals
   The Analects, which was written by his disciples, is still read today.
   I have a cat which can open the door by itself.

3) that — for people, things, or animals (more common in speech)
   This is the old temple that honours Confucius.
   She is the teacher that teaches us English.

Warning — don't double the subject!
   (✗) Confucius is a great teacher he lived 2,500 years ago.
   (✓) Confucius is a great teacher who lived 2,500 years ago.

Tip: in spoken English, we often use that in place of both who and which, especially when the information is essential.
lessons.cn:
定语从句告诉我们说的是哪个人或哪件事。通常紧跟在名词之后。

1) who——指人
   写这本书的老师来自上海。
   孔子是一位相信终身学习的哲学家。

2) which——指物或动物
   由弟子编成的《论语》至今仍被阅读。
   我有一只能自己开门的猫。

3) that——指人、物或动物（口语更常用）
   这是供奉孔子的古庙。
   她就是教我们英语的那位老师。

警告——不要重复主语！
   （✗）Confucius is a great teacher he lived 2,500 years ago.
   （✓）Confucius is a great teacher who lived 2,500 years ago.

小贴士：口语中常用 that 代替 who 和 which，尤其当信息不可省时。

lessons.title: More reading · Lessons from an old teacher
lessons.en:
Confucius never wrote a long book by himself. What we know about him comes from his students, who wrote down what he said and did. Below are three short lessons from The Analects that still matter today.

1) Learning is a joy.
"Is it not a pleasure to learn, and to put into practice what you have learned?" Confucius believed learning was not a burden, but a happy thing — as long as we use what we learn.

2) Friends are a treasure.
"Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant places?" At a time without phones or planes, a friend who travelled many days to visit was a real gift. Today, we may talk to friends online every day, but a real meeting is still something special.

3) Be kind; be fair.
A student once asked, "Is there a single word that can guide a person all his life?" Confucius replied, "Shu — do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself." This idea, later called the "Golden Rule," is found in almost every culture around the world.

A great thinker does not need to be rich or powerful. He only needs to share ideas that make ordinary people live better lives.
lessons.cn:
孔子自己没写过长篇大著。我们对他的了解都来自弟子——他们把他的言行记录下来。下面三则出自《论语》的短教诲至今仍有意义。

1) 学习是一种乐趣。
“学而时习之，不亦说乎？“孔子认为学习不是负担，而是快乐的事——只要能把学到的用出来。

2) 朋友是宝贝。
”有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎？”在没有电话和飞机的年代，好友跋涉多日来访就是一份真情厚礼。今天我们天天可以上网聊天，可真正的相见依旧难得。

3) 善良，公正。
有学生问：“有没有一个字能指引人的一生？”孔子答：“恕——己所不欲，勿施于人。”这条后来被称为“黄金法则”，几乎存在于世界上每一种文化之中。

伟大的思想家不必富有或有权，他只需分享让普通人过得更好的想法。

words.example: The light bulb is one of Edison's most famous inventions.
Marie Curie discovered two new elements: polonium and radium.
He failed the experiment a thousand times before it finally worked.
A curious mind is the first step towards any great discovery.
She spent long nights alone in the laboratory.
Great scientists are patient people.
Every failure is one step closer to success.
If at first you don't succeed, try again.
Einstein's theory changed the way we see time and space.
Winning the Nobel Prize was her greatest achievement.
Hard work is more important than talent alone.
She was determined to finish her research despite the difficulties.
He won first prize in the science contest.
Her life story inspires millions of young girls.
He made a great contribution to world peace.

lessons.title: Reading · Thomas Edison never gave up
lessons.en:
Reporter: Mr Edison, you have just given the world a useful electric light. People call you a genius. How do you feel?

Edison: A genius? I don't think so. I simply work very hard. The light bulb you see took me about 10,000 tries.

Reporter: Ten thousand failures? That sounds terrible!

Edison: I don't call them failures. I found 10,000 ways that didn't work, so I knew I was getting closer to the one that did.

Reporter: What gave you the courage to keep going?

Edison: Three things. First, I was curious about electricity since I was a boy. Curiosity is the starting point of every invention. Second, I had a team of people who believed in me. Third, I believed the world needed a clean, cheap light. That belief was stronger than my tiredness.

Reporter: Is it true that you slept only four hours a day?

Edison: Yes, when I was working on a problem. But I took short naps in the lab, on the desks, on the floor! A good nap is like a reset button.

Reporter: What advice do you have for young people who want to invent something?

Edison: Work hard, fail often, learn from every failure, and never stop being curious. Genius is one per cent inspiration and ninety-nine per cent perspiration.
lessons.cn:
记者：爱迪生先生，您给世界带来了实用的电灯，人们称您为天才，您有什么感想？

爱迪生：天才？我不这么认为，我只是非常努力。你看到的这个灯泡，花了我大约一万次尝试。

记者：一万次失败？听起来太糟糕了！

爱迪生：我不叫它们失败，我只是找到了一万种不可行的办法，这样我就知道离那条可行的路越来越近。

记者：是什么给您坚持下去的勇气？

爱迪生：三件事。第一，从小我就对电很好奇，好奇是每项发明的起点。第二，我有一支相信我的团队。第三，我坚信世界需要一种干净、便宜的光。这种信念比疲倦更强大。

记者：听说您每天只睡四小时，真的吗？

爱迪生：当我在攻关时是的。但我会在实验室打盹——桌子上、地板上都睡过！一次好盹就像按了重置键。

记者：对想搞发明的年轻人您有什么建议？

爱迪生：努力工作，频繁失败，从每次失败中学习，永远保持好奇。天才是百分之一的灵感加百分之九十九的汗水。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · Relative clauses with whose / where / when
lessons.en:
Some relative pronouns give extra information about people, places or times.

1) whose — shows possession (of people, animals, or even things)
   Edison is the inventor whose lab burnt down in 1914.
   I met a girl whose father is a scientist.

2) where — refers to a place (= in / at which)
   The laboratory where Curie worked was very cold in winter.
   Paris is the city where many great minds once lived.

3) when — refers to a time (= on / in which)
   1879 was the year when Edison produced a working light bulb.
   I still remember the day when the results were announced.

Compare:
   The house which Newton was born in is now a museum.  (which + preposition)
   The house where Newton was born is now a museum.    (where, shorter)

Both sentences are correct; where is simpler and more common in speech.
lessons.cn:
一些关系代词用来补充人、地点或时间的信息。

1) whose——表示所属（可指人、动物，甚至物）
   爱迪生是那位 1914 年实验室被烧毁的发明家。
   我遇到了一个父亲是科学家的女孩。

2) where——指地点（= in / at which）
   居里夫人工作的那间实验室冬天很冷。
   巴黎是许多伟大思想家曾生活过的城市。

3) when——指时间（= on / in which）
   1879 年是爱迪生造出可用灯泡的那一年。
   我仍记得公布成绩的那天。

比较：
   The house which Newton was born in is now a museum.（which + 介词）
   The house where Newton was born is now a museum.（where，更简洁）

两句都正确；口语更常用 where。

lessons.title: More reading · A woman who changed science
lessons.en:
When Marie Curie was a young girl in Poland, girls could not go to most universities. But her curiosity was stronger than any rule. Every night, after finishing her chores, she taught herself mathematics, physics and chemistry by candlelight.

At 24, she moved to Paris, where she was one of only a few women in the science faculty. She studied hard, but she had very little money. Sometimes she lived on bread and tea, because she wanted to buy books instead of food.

In Paris she met a shy scientist named Pierre Curie. They fell in love with ideas — and with each other. They shared a small, cold laboratory and worked as a team for years. In 1898, they discovered two new elements and named one of them polonium, after Marie's homeland.

Marie Curie was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize, and the first person to win it twice — once for physics (1903) and once for chemistry (1911). She used her prize money not to buy a bigger house, but to build better laboratories.

She once said, "Nothing in life is to be feared; it is only to be understood." Her life shows that a curious, determined mind can break any door, even one marked "No girls allowed."
lessons.cn:
玛丽·居里年少时住在波兰，当时大多数大学不收女生。但她的好奇心比任何规定都强。每晚做完家务，她就靠烛光自学数学、物理、化学。

24 岁那年，她来到巴黎，成为理学院少数女生之一。她学得刻苦，却非常贫穷，有时只靠面包和茶度日，因为她宁愿买书也不愿买食物。

在巴黎她遇见了一位害羞的科学家——皮埃尔·居里。他们因理想相爱，也彼此相爱。夫妻俩在一间又小又冷的实验室并肩工作多年。1898 年他们发现了两种新元素，其中一种以玛丽的祖国命名为钋。

居里夫人是首位获得诺贝尔奖的女性，也是首位两度获奖的人——1903 年物理奖、1911 年化学奖。她用奖金不是换大房子，而是建更好的实验室。

她曾说：“人生没有什么可怕的事，只有要去理解的事。”她的一生证明：一颗好奇而坚定的心，能推开任何一扇门，哪怕门上写着“女生止步”。

words.example: We must protect the environment for future generations.
Air pollution in big cities is a serious problem.
Plastic waste damages the oceans.
Don't waste water — every drop counts.
We should reduce the use of plastic bags.
Paper and glass can be recycled easily.
We did a survey on our neighbourhood's green habits.
Please fill in this short questionnaire.
Our neighbourhood is quiet and clean.
Sort your rubbish before you throw it away.
Put empty bottles into the blue bin.
Every citizen should care about the city.
Public transport is both green and cheap.
Fires destroyed huge areas of forest last year.
We must protect our rivers from pollution.

lessons.title: Reading · A survey on our neighbourhood
lessons.en:
Teacher: Good afternoon, class. Last week you did a survey on our neighbourhood. Who wants to share the results?

Betty: I'll start. Our group asked 50 people how they throw away their rubbish.

Teacher: And what did you find?

Betty: Only 18 people sort their rubbish into three bins — paper, plastic and kitchen waste. The other 32 people put everything into one bag!

Jim: Our group studied noise. We stood near the main road from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m.

Teacher: How bad was it?

Jim: Too noisy to talk! The loudest moment was 85 decibels — as loud as a vacuum cleaner. Most of the noise came from car horns.

Lucy: My group looked at the small park on Lotus Street. We counted the people who came in during one hour.

Teacher: How many?

Lucy: 64 people — most of them old people and children. We asked them what they liked and what they didn't. They loved the flowers, but hated the broken benches and the rubbish near the gate.

Teacher: Wonderful work. So, are there any ideas for solutions?

Betty: Our class could make colourful posters about sorting rubbish.

Jim: We could write a letter to ask drivers not to press their horns too much.

Lucy: And we could spend one Saturday cleaning the park and fixing the benches with our parents.

Teacher: Perfect. A good survey is not the end — it is the start of real action.
lessons.cn:
老师：下午好，同学们。上周你们对社区做了调查。谁想先分享结果？

贝蒂：我先来。我们组问了 50 人怎样扔垃圾。

老师：结果如何？

贝蒂：只有 18 人把垃圾分成纸、塑料和厨余三类；另外 32 人全部装一袋！

吉姆：我们组研究噪声，早上 7 点到 9 点站在主干道旁。

老师：情况糟吗？

吉姆：吵到没法说话！最高 85 分贝，跟吸尘器一样响。噪声主要来自汽车喇叭。

露西：我们组观察莲花街小公园，数了一小时进出的人数。

老师：多少？

露西：64 人——多数是老人和小孩。我们问他们喜欢与不喜欢什么。他们喜欢花，却讨厌坏掉的长椅和门口的垃圾。

老师：做得好。大家有什么解决办法？

贝蒂：我们可以做彩色海报，宣传垃圾分类。

吉姆：可以写信请司机不要随意按喇叭。

露西：也可以用一个周六，和爸妈一起清理公园、修好长椅。

老师：完美。好的调查不是终点，而是真正行动的起点。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · too ... to ... and so ... that ...
lessons.en:
Both structures show degree, but they look and feel different.

1) too + adj./adv. + to + verb → too ... to do something
   The river is too dirty to swim in.
   He spoke too fast for me to understand.
   Often suggests a NEGATIVE result (cannot / couldn't).

2) so + adj./adv. + that + clause → so ... that ...
   The river is so dirty that we cannot swim in it.
   He spoke so fast that I could not understand him.
   The result clause uses that + a full sentence.

3) so many / so much / so few / so little + noun + that ...
   There is so much rubbish on the beach that we cannot walk freely.
   So few birds come here now that the forest feels empty.

Change one to the other:
   The air is too bad to breathe.  →  The air is so bad that we cannot breathe.
   She is so young that she can't join the club.  →  She is too young to join the club.

Remember: too ... to ... already contains a NEGATIVE meaning — never add not after to.
lessons.cn:
两种结构都表示程度，外形与语感不同。

1) too + 形容词/副词 + to + 动词 → 太……以至于不能……
   河水太脏，不能游泳。
   他说得太快，我听不懂。
   通常表达否定结果（不能／无法）。

2) so + 形容词/副词 + that + 从句 → 如此……以至于……
   河水太脏，以至于我们不能游泳。
   他说得太快，以至于我听不懂。
   结果部分用 that + 完整句。

3) so many / so much / so few / so little + 名词 + that ...
   海滩上垃圾太多，以至于无法自由行走。
   现在来这里的鸟太少，森林都显得空荡。

互换练习：
   The air is too bad to breathe. → The air is so bad that we cannot breathe.
   She is so young that she can't join the club. → She is too young to join the club.

注意：too ... to ... 本身已含否定义，to 后不能再加 not。

lessons.title: More reading · One city, three smaller worries
lessons.en:
Every big city has big stories — tall buildings, bright lights, fast trains. But underneath, there are three smaller worries that people often ignore.

Worry 1: Plastic snow.
In many city parks, tiny pieces of plastic lie among the grass like snow. They come from bottles, bags, and even clothes. When it rains, this "plastic snow" washes into rivers and then into the sea. Scientists now find plastic pieces in fish, salt, and even tap water. The plastic snow of today is the plastic food of tomorrow.

Worry 2: Light that never sleeps.
Street lights, screens, neon signs — a big city never goes dark. This is useful, but it also confuses animals. Young sea turtles, for example, once followed the moonlight to the sea. Now they follow the city lights and die on the road. Birds, too, lose their way during long night flights.

Worry 3: Seconds of silence.
People say cities are loud, but the real problem is that they never go quiet. Even at midnight, we hear cars, air-conditioners and construction. Scientists say constant low noise can hurt a child's memory and a grown-up's heart. A few minutes of real quiet every day is as important as a glass of water.

These worries are small for each person, but huge for the city. A city is a long story written by many citizens. If we each write one kind sentence, the story can have a happy ending.
lessons.cn:
每座大城市都有大故事——高楼、霓虹、疾驰的列车。但在表面之下，有三个常被忽视的小烦恼。

烦恼一：塑料雪。
许多城市公园的草地上，散落着如雪般的小塑料碎片，它们来自瓶子、袋子甚至衣物。一场雨后，这些“塑料雪”被冲进河流，再流向大海。科学家已在鱼、盐乃至自来水中发现塑料颗粒。今天的塑料雪，就是明天的塑料食物。

烦恼二：不眠的灯。
路灯、屏幕、霓虹——大城市从不天黑。这虽方便，却让动物迷茫。幼海龟曾追随月光走向大海，如今却随着城市灯光走上公路、丧命途中。候鸟夜飞时也常因光污染迷失方向。

烦恼三：难得的安静。
人们常说城市吵闹，其实真正的问题是永不安静。即使午夜，汽车、空调、施工声不断。科学家指出，持续的低噪音会伤害孩子的记忆和成人的心脏。每天几分钟真正的安静，和一杯水同样重要。

这些烦恼于个人微小，于城市却巨大。城市是一部由众多居民书写的长故事，若每人写下一句善意的话，结局就能温暖而美好。

words.example: There is no simple solution to climate change.
Climate change is a global problem.
Global warming melts the ice in the Arctic.
Cars release a lot of carbon every day.
We must cut carbon emissions by half.
Solar energy is clean and free.
Wind is a renewable energy source.
Our school has solar panels on the roof.
More and more buses are now electric.
Every year, huge forests are cut down for paper.
Many species are disappearing because of habitat loss.
Without action, pandas could one day become extinct.
Most rubbish ends up in a huge landfill.
Our school started a campaign called Zero Plastic Week.
Fifty volunteers joined the tree-planting day.

lessons.title: Reading · Small steps save the planet
lessons.en:
Dear students,

We are writing to every class in our school to launch a month-long campaign called "Small Steps, Big Planet". Climate change is not a problem for some far-away country — it is happening here, in our city, in our school, in our homes.

Last summer, it was so hot that our school closed for two extra days. Last winter, heavy rain flooded the shops near the station. Trees on the mountain are being cut, and birds that used to sing in our gardens are slowly disappearing.

These problems feel huge. But the good news is that every small step counts. Here are four ideas for our school community:

1) Green classrooms. Turn off the lights and fans when you leave. A class that does this every day can save enough electricity to light 30 homes for a week.

2) Lunch without waste. Bring your own bottle and chopsticks. Finish your food; food waste in landfills produces a gas that traps heat in the sky.

3) Green wheels. Walk, cycle, or take the bus whenever you can. Ask a parent to drive together with a friend — two families, one car.

4) Green voices. Tell your family the new facts you learn. A child who talks about the planet can change a whole home.

It is not the biggest hero who saves the world. It is millions of ordinary people doing small, kind things, every day. Join us. Take one small step today — and tomorrow, another.

Yours truly,
The Environment Club
lessons.cn:
亲爱的同学们：

我们向全校各班发出倡议，启动为期一个月的“小步伐，大地球”运动。气候变化不是远方的事——它正发生在我们的城市、学校、家里。

去年夏天太热，学校多放了两天假；去年冬天大雨淹了车站附近的商店；山上的树被砍，花园里曾经歌唱的鸟渐渐不见。

这些问题看似巨大，好消息是每一小步都算数。以下是四个校园建议：

1) 绿色教室：离开时关灯、关风扇。一个班每天坚持，省下的电够 30 个家庭用一周。

2) 零浪费午餐：自带水瓶筷子，吃完饭菜。食物烂在填埋场会产生让天空变热的气体。

3) 绿色车轮：能走就走，能骑就骑，能坐公交就坐公交。请爸妈和朋友拼车——两家一辆车。

4) 绿色声音：把学到的新知识讲给家人。一个谈地球的孩子，能改变整个家。

拯救世界的不是最大的英雄，而是千百万普通人每天做的小而善的事。加入我们吧。今天迈一小步，明天再一步。

环保社敬上

lessons.title: Grammar focus · The emphatic pattern "It is ... that / who ..."
lessons.en:
When we want to focus on one part of a sentence, we can use the pattern:
   It is / was + EMPHASISED PART + that / who + the rest of the sentence.

The emphasised part can be:

1) The subject (use who for people, that for things):
   Tom broke the window.  →  It was Tom who / that broke the window.
   Plastic pollutes the sea.  →  It is plastic that pollutes the sea.

2) The object:
   We need clean water most.  →  It is clean water that we need most.

3) A time or place (use that, NOT when / where):
   We started the campaign last Monday.  →  It was last Monday that we started the campaign.
   I first met her in Shanghai.  →  It was in Shanghai that I first met her.

Questions:
   Was it Tom who broke the window?
   Who was it that broke the window?

NOT-form:
   It was NOT Tom who broke the window; it was Jim.

Important: the rest of the sentence keeps its normal tense — do not change the second verb to "is".
lessons.cn:
强调句把句子的一部分突出出来：
   It is / was + 强调部分 + that / who + 其余部分。

强调部分可以是：

1) 主语（指人用 who，指物用 that）：
   Tom broke the window. → It was Tom who / that broke the window.
   Plastic pollutes the sea. → It is plastic that pollutes the sea.

2) 宾语：
   We need clean water most. → It is clean water that we need most.

3) 时间或地点（一律用 that，不用 when / where）：
   We started the campaign last Monday. → It was last Monday that we started the campaign.
   I first met her in Shanghai. → It was in Shanghai that I first met her.

疑问：
   Was it Tom who broke the window?
   Who was it that broke the window?

否定：
   It was NOT Tom who broke the window; it was Jim.

重要：其余部分保留原时态，不要把第二个动词改成 is。

lessons.title: More reading · Three cities, three green answers
lessons.en:
No single city has all the answers, but many cities around the world are trying brave experiments. Here are three stories.

Freiburg, Germany — The Sun City.
Thirty years ago, Freiburg was a quiet old town. Today, it is one of the greenest cities in Europe. Every new house must save energy; many roofs are covered with solar panels. Streets belong to people first, cars second. Children learn about wind and sun in primary school. The city now makes more clean energy than it uses.

Curitiba, Brazil — The Bus City.
In the 1970s, Curitiba was growing fast and its roads were full of cars. Instead of building more highways, the city built long, fast bus lines. Today, 70 out of every 100 people in Curitiba take the bus every day — more than in almost any other Brazilian city. The city also pays poor families to collect and sort rubbish; a bag of paper equals a basket of vegetables.

Kitakyushu, Japan — The River City.
After the war, Kitakyushu grew many factories and its main river turned black. Fish died; children fell sick. Mothers went on strike until the city acted. Fifty years later, the river runs clear, and fish have returned. Old factories are museums. Children swim in summer, and a nearby beach welcomes sea turtles every spring.

Each of these cities shows that it is strong citizens who push cities to change. A city that listens to its people becomes a home worth living in.
lessons.cn:
没有一座城市拥有所有答案，但全球许多城市都在大胆尝试。下面三段故事。

德国弗赖堡——太阳之城。
三十年前它还是安静小城，如今已是欧洲最绿之一。所有新房须节能，屋顶普遍铺太阳能板；街道先让人，再让车；孩子在小学就学风能与太阳能。城市所产清洁电力已超出所需。

巴西库里蒂巴——公交之城。
上世纪 70 年代城市迅猛扩张，道路拥堵。它不修更多公路，而是铺下长长的快速公交专线。如今每 100 人里 70 人每天乘公交，比大多数巴西城市都高。市政府还用蔬菜换贫困家庭捡来的分类垃圾：一袋废纸换一篮青菜。

日本北九州——河流之城。
战后大量工厂兴起，主河变成黑水，鱼死、孩子病倒。母亲们罢工抗议，市政府终于行动。五十年后，河水清澈，鱼群归来；老工厂改成博物馆；孩子夏天在河里游泳，附近海滩每年春天迎来海龟。

三座城市告诉我们：是坚强的市民推动城市改变。懂得倾听人民的城市，才能成为值得居住的家园。

lessons.title: Reading · Two films worth watching
lessons.en:
Jenny: Hi, Peter. I watched two great films this weekend. You should see them too.

Peter: Sounds good. What are they about?

Jenny: The first one is called Hi, Mom. It is a Chinese family comedy, but it has a deep heart. A young woman travels back in time and meets her own mother when her mother was still a girl.

Peter: That's an interesting idea. Who is the director?

Jenny: Jia Ling. She wrote it and directed it herself. The film is based on her own mother's life. Over 50 million tickets were sold in China during the first month.

Peter: Wow. And the second film?

Jenny: The second is The Wandering Earth II, a Chinese science fiction film. Humans must move our planet to a new star because the sun is dying. The special effects were made by more than 1,000 artists, and some scenes were shot in the Gobi Desert.

Peter: How long is it?

Jenny: About three hours, but I didn't feel sleepy for a minute! The music was written by a famous Chinese composer, and the main actor spoke in a calm, powerful voice.

Peter: Are they suitable for my little brother?

Jenny: Hi, Mom is perfect for family viewing. The Wandering Earth II has some scary scenes, so kids under 10 may need a parent nearby.

Peter: Thanks. I'll book seats for Saturday. A good film is a ticket to a new world.
lessons.cn:
珍妮：嗨，彼得。这周末我看了两部好片，你也该去看。

彼得：好啊，讲什么的？

珍妮：第一部叫《你好，李焕英》，一部中国家庭喜剧，却很动人。一位年轻女子穿越时空，遇见少女时代的妈妈。

彼得：立意很有意思。导演是谁？

珍妮：贾玲，她自编自导自演，灵感源自自己的母亲。影片上映首月就卖出五千多万张票。

彼得：厉害！第二部呢？

珍妮：第二部是《流浪地球 2》，中国科幻片。因太阳快死，人类要把地球推向新的恒星。特效由一千多位艺术家完成，部分镜头在戈壁拍摄。

彼得：多长？

珍妮：约三小时，但我一秒都没犯困！配乐由中国名作曲家创作，男主角声音沉稳有力。

彼得：适合我弟弟看吗？

珍妮：《你好，李焕英》很适合家庭观看；《流浪地球 2》有惊险场面，10 岁以下小孩最好有家长陪同。

彼得：谢啦，我订周六的票。好电影就是通往新世界的车票。

lessons.title: Grammar focus · The passive voice (simple present and simple past)
lessons.en:
We use the passive voice when we want to focus on the thing or person that receives the action — not who does the action.

Form:
   subject + am / is / are + past participle   (present)
   subject + was / were + past participle      (past)

Active → Passive
   They sell tickets online.         →  Tickets are sold online.
   Jia Ling directed the film.       →  The film was directed by Jia Ling.
   Thousands of fans loved the hero. →  The hero was loved by thousands of fans.

By + doer (optional):
Only add "by + doer" when the doer is important or surprising. If the doer is obvious or unknown, leave it out.
   The film was released last Friday.   (everyone knows the cinema released it)
   The building was built in 1925.     (we don't know who)
   The cake was eaten by the dog!      (surprise!)

Common verbs that have irregular past participles:
   write → written   speak → spoken   sing → sung
   take → taken     break → broken   make → made

Questions and negatives:
   Was the film directed by Jia Ling? Yes, it was.
   The story was not written in a hurry.
lessons.cn:
当我们关心“被动作”的对象，而非“动作执行者”时，用被动语态。

形式：
   主语 + am / is / are + 过去分词（现在）
   主语 + was / were + 过去分词（过去）

主动 → 被动
   They sell tickets online. → Tickets are sold online.
   Jia Ling directed the film. → The film was directed by Jia Ling.
   Thousands of fans loved the hero. → The hero was loved by thousands of fans.

by + 动作执行者（可选）：
只有在执行者重要或令人意外时才加 by。执行者显而易见或不明时可省。
   The film was released last Friday.（默认是电影院）
   The building was built in 1925.（不知是谁建的）
   The cake was eaten by the dog!（意外）

常见不规则过去分词：
   write → written    speak → spoken    sing → sung
   take → taken      break → broken    make → made

疑问与否定：
   Was the film directed by Jia Ling? Yes, it was.
   The story was not written in a hurry.

lessons.title: More reading · A hundred years of Chinese film
lessons.en:
Chinese film has a long and proud history. The first Chinese film, Conquering Jun Mountain, was made in 1905 in a small photo studio in Beijing. It was only about ten minutes long, but it was loved by the emperor's family.

In the 1930s, Shanghai became the capital of Chinese cinema. Films about ordinary city life were produced in large numbers, and young actors such as Ruan Lingyu became stars overnight.

After 1949, films from northern China focused on farmers, soldiers and factory workers. Songs from these films — like "My Motherland" — are still sung by grandparents today.

The 1980s brought a new wave. Directors such as Chen Kaige and Zhang Yimou used strong colours and slow, quiet stories to win international awards. The film Raise the Red Lantern was nominated for an Oscar in 1992.

After 2000, Chinese cinema grew faster than ever. Kung-fu films, comedies, love stories and science fiction are all produced each year. In 2023, the box office of Chinese-made films reached over 40 billion yuan — most tickets were bought by young audiences aged 18 to 35.

More importantly, Chinese films are now shown in over 100 countries. A good film is not only a story; it is a window through which the world sees our hearts.
lessons.cn:
中国电影历史悠久、成就斐然。中国第一部电影《定军山》拍摄于 1905 年，北京一家照相馆里完成，只有十分钟长，却深受皇室喜爱。

上世纪 30 年代，上海成为中国电影之都。大量表现城市百姓生活的影片被拍出来，阮玲玉等年轻演员一夜成名。

1949 年后，北方电影聚焦农民、军人和工人。像《我的祖国》这样的电影插曲，至今仍被爷爷奶奶传唱。

80 年代迎来新浪潮。陈凯歌、张艺谋等导演以浓烈色彩与缓慢叙事屡获国际大奖。《大红灯笼高高挂》1992 年获奥斯卡提名。

2000 年以后，中国电影发展迅猛，每年都有功夫片、喜剧、爱情片与科幻片问世。2023 年国产片票房超过 400 亿元，大多数票由 18 到 35 岁的年轻观众购买。

更重要的是，中国电影如今在 100 多个国家上映。好电影不仅是故事，更是世界通过它看见我们内心的窗口。

Thousands of fans went to her concert last night.
The audience cheered loudly at the end.

The lights on the stage turned blue and gold.

Tonight's performance was absolutely amazing.
